name: Drive-by Compromise
description:
Adversaries may gain access to a system during a drive-by compromise, when a user visits a website as part of a regular browsing session. With this technique, the user's web browser is targeted and exploited simply by visiting the compromised website. 

The adversary may target a specific community, such as trusted third party suppliers or other industry specific groups, which often visit the target website. This kind of targeted attack relies on a common interest, and is known as a strategic web compromise or watering hole attack. 

The National Cyber Awareness System (NCAS) has issued a Technical Alert (TA) regarding Russian government cyber activity targeting critical infrastructure sectors. (Citation: Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency March 2018) Analysis by DHS and FBI has noted two distinct categories of victims in the Dragonfly campaign on the Western energy sector: staging and intended targets. The adversary targeted the less secure networks of staging targets, including trusted third-party suppliers and related peripheral organizations. Initial access to the intended targets used watering hole attacks to target process control, ICS, and critical infrastructure related trade publications and informational websites.

references.description: Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency 2018, March 15 Alert (TA18-074A) Russian Government Cyber Activity Targeting Energy and Other Critical Infrastructure Sectors Retrieved. 2019/10/11

telemetry.name: Application Log Content
telemetry.description: Application-emitted audit or operational event content.
telemetry.collection_focus: Select the application event family required by the detection and document its native schema before normalization.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.name: Process Creation
telemetry.description: Creation of a process with executable, command line, parent and security context.
telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

providers.name: Microsoft Sysmon
providers.scope: Windows event-based collection; enable the event types needed below.

providers.name: Linux Audit
providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

providers.name: Apple Endpoint Security clients
providers.scope: macOS alternative where the subscribed event exists; requires an entitled, approved client, not an iOS collector.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

configuration_example.label: Sysmon filter fragment · merge into the reviewed lab configuration
configuration_example.note: This fragment only selects the named process. It is not a complete production policy. Inspect the installed schema with sysmon64 -s; preserve existing rules, then apply the reviewed complete configuration with sysmon64 -c <configuration-file>.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Event filtering and sensor versions change coverage. High-volume image-load and process-access collection needs tuning; endpoint events alone do not establish intent.

sources.title: Apple Endpoint Security framework for macOS

telemetry.anomaly_design: Per host role and user: rare process/object combinations, bursts of object access or modification, and ordered parent/action sequences. Compare maintenance windows and signed software rollout activity.

analytics.name: Analytic 1914
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a browser process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) workstation spawning an unexpected child process immediately following navigation to an external website, particularly a vendor support or software-download site. Documented Havex precedent: adversaries compromised legitimate ICS vendor websites to serve trojanized software downloads. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

tuning.description: Inventory of ICS engineering/operator workstations from which routine vendor software downloads occur.

log_sources.name: webproxy:applog
log_sources.channel: file download from domain not matching verified vendor Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate/domain history, immediately preceding the anomalous process spawn

log_sources.name: WinEventLog:Sysmon
log_sources.channel: EventCode=1 where a browser process spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, wscript.exe, or another executable outside the approved browser-child baseline

analytics.name: Analytic 2147
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a browser process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux workstation spawning child processes that execute with arguments inconsistent with normal browsing, or writing binaries to /tmp or user home directories. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the account/device/session violates the approved identity + source host/jump path/zone policy and is corroborated by access to a protected OT asset, execution, configuration change, or another security-relevant follow-on event. Suppress approved shift activity, vendor support, break-glass use, commissioning, and documented remote-access windows.

tuning.description: Inventory of ICS engineering/operator workstations from which routine vendor software downloads occur.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: Linux Audit SYSCALL/EXECVE/SOCKADDR records (configured audit rule): syscall=execve; browser process spawns a command shell, script interpreter, or executable child inconsistent with the approved browser-child baseline

software.name: Bad Rabbit
software.description: [Bad Rabbit](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0606) ransomware spreads through drive-by attacks where insecure websites are compromised. While the target is visiting a legitimate website, a malware dropper is being downloaded from the threat actors infrastructure. (Citation: Orkhan Mamedov, Fedor Sinitsyn, Anton Ivanov October 2017)

actors.name: Dragonfly
actors.description: [Dragonfly](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0035) utilized watering hole attacks on energy sector websites by injecting a redirect iframe to deliver [Backdoor.Oldrea](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0093) or [Trojan.Karagany](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0094). (Citation: Symantec Security Response July 2014)

references.description: Symantec Security Response 2014, July 7 Dragonfly: Cyberespionage Attacks Against Energy Suppliers Retrieved. 2016/04/08

actors.name: OilRig
actors.description: [OilRig](https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0049) has been seen utilizing watering hole attacks to collect credentials which could be used to gain access into ICS networks. (Citation: Eduard Kovacs May 2018)

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.description: Restrict browsers to limit the capabilities of malicious ads and Javascript.

mitigations.name: Application Isolation and Sandboxing
mitigations.description: Built-in browser sandboxes and application isolation may be used to contain web-based malware.

mitigations.name: Exploit Protection
mitigations.description: Utilize exploit protection to prevent activities which may be exploited through malicious web sites.

mitigations.name: Update Software
mitigations.description: Ensure all browsers and plugins are kept updated to help prevent the exploit phase of this technique. Use modern browsers with security features enabled.

simulation.prerequisites: Use a process simulator or isolated test rig with no connection to production controllers or physical actuators. Preserve safety interlocks; destructive effects require synthetic evidence, not real equipment damage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
